note: Traced on OSM roads (Valhalla); dirtPct from OSM surface; fuelGap from OSM fuel stations within 3 km. Check closures before riding.

routes.notes: Washboard and potholes, steep switchbacks near the summit; snow until June; logging trucks on weekdays.

routes.n: Carpenter Lake Road (Lillooet to Gold Bridge)
routes.notes: Narrow canyon road with drop-offs and rockfall; pairs with the Hurley for a loop.

routes.n: Duffey Lake Road (Hwy 99, Pemberton to Lillooet)
routes.notes: Paved, 13% grades and tight hairpins; frequent winter closures.

routes.n: Harrison West and In-SHUCK-ch FSR (Harrison Mills to Mount Currie)
routes.notes: Remote logging roads along Harrison and Lillooet lakes; washouts after rain, no services between ends.
Narrow gravel above the Fraser; ends at the Lytton reaction ferry (free, check it is running).

routes.n: Dog Creek Road (Williams Lake to Clinton)
routes.notes: Fraser grasslands gravel through Alkali Lake, Dog Creek and Jesmond; clay is slick when wet.

routes.n: Farwell Canyon and Big Creek loop
routes.notes: Hoodoos and sand dunes in the canyon; steep loose descent to the Chilcotin River bridge.

routes.n: Freedom Highway (Hwy 20, Williams Lake to Bella Coola)
routes.notes: The Hill: 18% gravel grades and hairpins with no guardrails; ferry from Bella Coola to Port Hardy in summer.
Cariboo gold-rush logging roads; signage is poor, carry a map.

routes.n: Hwy 31 Lardeau and Trout Lake (Kaslo to Revelstoke)
routes.notes: Gravel north of Gerrard; free Upper Arrow Lake ferry Galena Bay to Shelter Bay.
Paved; two free ferries (Kootenay Lake, Upper Arrow Lake), sailings fill on summer weekends.
Mostly paved with gravel patches and no shoulders; bears and long fuel gaps, fill at every stop.

routes.n: Stewart, Hyder and Salmon Glacier road
routes.notes: Gravel past Hyder (Alaska, no US check going in, Canada customs on return); snow at the summit into July.
20% gravel grades on a narrow lava ridge above the Stikine; fire-damaged area, ask in Dease Lake first.
Mostly paved now with gravel patches; dead end at Atlin, fuel there is limited hours.
Logging mainline being chip-sealed in sections; expect gravel, construction and trucks.

routes.n: Head Bay Road (Gold River to Tahsis)
routes.notes: Steep, narrow logging road to the west coast; potholes and loose rock.

routes.n: Holberg Road to San Josef Bay
routes.notes: Logging mainline to Cape Scott park; check WFP road hours, no fuel past Port Hardy.
Gravel past Osprey Lake, cattle on the road; good link from the Similkameen to the Okanagan.
Old mining towns, gravel from Tulameen to Brookmere; dusty in August.

routes.n: Flathead FSR (Morrissey to the Flathead Valley)
routes.notes: Dead end near the closed Montana border; grizzly country, no services.

routes.n: Forestry Trunk Road South (Coleman to Highwood)
routes.notes: 99 km of gravel through the Livingstone range; no fuel, wind is strong.

routes.n: Forestry Trunk Road (Hwy 734, Sundre to Nordegg)
routes.notes: Gravel past Ram Falls; random camping on Crown land needs a Public Lands Camping Pass.

routes.n: Forestry Trunk Road North (Hwy 40 to Hwy 43)
routes.notes: Remote industrial gravel with fast trucks; no fuel for the whole section.

routes.n: Smith-Dorrien Spray Trail (Canmore to Kananaskis Lakes)
routes.notes: Gravel through Kananaskis; Kananaskis Conservation Pass needed to park, wildlife on the road.

routes.n: Ya Ha Tinda road (Sundre to the Red Deer River)
routes.notes: Gravel dead end to the Parks Canada horse ranch; elk herds, no services.
Sand and gravel to a closed uranium mine; no fuel or services past La Loche.
Gravel north of Missinipe through boreal lakes; wildfire closures in summer.
Mine-traffic gravel to the end of the all-weather road; carry fuel and a satellite messenger.
Rough gravel with deep potholes after rain; fuel only at Split Lake and Gillam.
Long boreal road with gravel sections; fuel at Leaf Rapids.

routes.n: Nopiming PR 314 (Lac du Bonnet to Bissett)
routes.notes: Gravel through Canadian Shield lakes in Nopiming park; dusty and narrow.
Gravel over the Manitoba escarpment past Wellman and Childs lakes.
Paved, twisty Mississagi River road; one fuel stop at Wharncliffe area is seasonal.
Long logging gravel with fast trucks and dust; no services.

routes.n: Lake Nipigon west side (Hwy 527 to Gull Bay and Armstrong)
routes.notes: Remote paved Hwy 527 with a short gravel spur to Gull Bay; gravel bush roads continue past Armstrong.
Paved but Ontario's most remote highway; fuel at Savant Lake only.

routes.n: Route de la Baie-James (Matagami to Radisson)
routes.notes: Paved; register at the km 6 stop; fuel only at km 381 Relais.

routes.n: Route du Nord (Chibougamau to Baie-James km 275)
routes.notes: Long gravel through Eeyou Istchee; fuel at Nemaska only.
Remote gravel with sharp rock; one fuel stop at the Mirage outfitter, carry spare tubes and fuel.
Paved south, gravel near Fire Lake; mine trucks, fuel at Manic-5 and Relais Gabriel.

routes.n: Route 167 Nord to the Otish Mountains
routes.notes: Gravel past Mistissini toward the Renard mine; public road but no services.
Paved mountain crossing through Gaspésie park; moose at dusk, no fuel inside the park.

routes.n: Route 138 to Kegaska (end of the road)
routes.notes: Paved Côte-Nord to the last village; continue by the Bella Desgagnés coastal ferry.

routes.n: Trans-Labrador Highway (Labrador City to Goose Bay)
routes.notes: Paved since 2022 but remote; free satellite phone loan program, fuel at Churchill Falls.
Longest fuel gap in Canada to Port Hope Simpson; ferry Blanc-Sablon to St. Barbe.

routes.n: Viking Trail (Route 430, Deer Lake to St. Anthony)
routes.notes: Paved through Gros Morne; strong coastal wind and moose.
Paved loop with a gravel cliff-edge spur to Meat Cove; park pass needed in the highlands.
Quiet paved road into the Maritimes' highest hills; no fuel between Plaster Rock and Saint-Quentin.

routes.n: PEI red clay Scenic Heritage Roads
routes.notes: Short unpaved red clay lanes linked by quiet paved roads; greasy and rutted after rain.
Shale gravel shreds tires; Peel and Mackenzie ferries (no crossing at freeze-up and break-up); fuel at Eagle Plains.
Gravel on permafrost, soft and muddy when wet; Tuk fuel is limited hours.

routes.n: Top of the World Highway (Dawson to Alaska)
routes.notes: George Black ferry from Dawson; border only open mid May to mid September, daytime.
Narrow, winding single-lane gravel with old one-lane bridges; no services.

routes.n: North Canol Road (Ross River to Macmillan Pass)
routes.notes: Rough, washouts and creek fords; Ross River ferry, dead end at the NWT border.

routes.n: Robert Campbell Highway (Watson Lake to Carmacks)
routes.notes: Gravel most of the way; fuel at Ross River and Faro, check hours.

routes.n: Silver Trail (Stewart Crossing to Keno City)
routes.notes: Paved to Mayo then gravel; climb Keno Hill road for the view (rough).
Unmaintained past km 134 with washouts and overgrown bridges; no services, satellite messenger.
Gravel that turns to greasy clay in rain; fuel only in Fort Liard.
Gravel along the Mackenzie with the Camsell Bend ferry; no fuel until Wrigley.
Paved then gravel past Prelude Lake; start of the winter road to the diamond mines.
